title: The Doldrums
intro_lines: Third day of no wind.
The sail hangs like wet laundry.
The sea is a hot coin. Your tongue sticks to your teeth.

choices.label: Ration the water. Sit still.

outcomes.text: You stretch the last of the water past noon. Hunger gnaws, but heads stay clear.
A squall line darkens the west by dusk. You wring rain out of the sail into a shell.
Heatstroke takes you. Tide-Puck licks your face until you sit up and vomit bile.

choices.label: Strip and slip over the side to cool.

outcomes.text: The water is cooler than the air and holds you up. You climb back steady.
Something large passes beneath, close enough to lift the raft an inch.
A cramp locks your leg. You claw back aboard, swallowing salt, coughing.

choices.label: Cut a paddle and row for the cloud bank.

outcomes.text: Four hours of rowing buys a mile and a breeze that smells of rain to come.
The cloud bank is empty. You burn water you could not spare on a lie.
You find a current line, cool and moving. It carries you north all afternoon.

history_note: Rule of threes: roughly three days without water, and shade and water come before food — Serrano was driven into the sea by sunburn before thirst ever bit.

title: A Sail With No Colours
intro_lines: A dinghy slides out of the fog: one oar, one man.
He ships the oar and holds up a cracked clay jug.
"Water for passage," he says. "I mean no trouble."

choices.label: Share water and take him aboard.

outcomes.text: He drinks, then bails for an hour without being asked. The raft rides higher.
He drinks. His eyes keep going to the knife stuck in your sailcloth.
He drinks, thanks you, and rows off into the fog without another word.

choices.label: Keep him at oar's length. Trade nothing.

outcomes.text: He shrugs and pulls away. The fog takes him. You never learn his name.
He curses you in three languages and rows off. Tide-Puck growls at his wake.
He leaves a floating cask behind him, then vanishes into the grey.

choices.label: Take the jug, give him nothing.

outcomes.text: The jug is rainwater, flat but clean. He watches you drink and says nothing.
He snatches the jug back and is gone before you can get your feet under you.
The jug is brine with a rag stuffed in the neck. A joke, or a test, or both.

history_note: Ships sighted Pedro Serrano's smoke for years but stayed clear of the shoals around his cay.

title: The Current Runs Wrong
intro_lines: The water has gone the colour of old brass.
Your drift line pulls sideways, then hard.
Ahead, white water breaks in a long, even line.

choices.label: Paddle across the current, not against

outcomes.text: You angle out and the current spits you clear of the breakers, cursing.
Half a mile of hard pulling. Your palms open and bleed onto the shaft.
You misjudge the angle. A breaker swamps the raft and takes your spare timber.

choices.label: Ride it in and beach on the reef's lee.

outcomes.text: You take the crest, slam down, and spin into calm water behind the coral.
Coral opens the raft's lashing. You bail with your hands and hold it together.
The raft comes apart. You swim for the coral shelf with Tide-Puck on your shoulder.

choices.label: Throw the sea anchor and wait it out.

outcomes.text: The anchor bites. You hold station all night and the current slackens with the tide.
The line parts at dawn. You lose the anchor and a whole night with it.
The current drags you sideways over the shelf. Something scrapes underneath.

history_note: Tromelin's rescue boats were smashed on the reef twice — castaways learned a reef is a wall you cross once, on purpose, at the right tide.

title: Barrels in the Wake
intro_lines: Half a mile off, barrels bob in a loose string.
One is stencilled: UTC — NAVAL VICTUALLER.
Two are stove in. One still rides high.

choices.label: Row out and take the sound one.

outcomes.text: Salt pork, hard tack, a sealed jar of tar. A good day, for once.
The barrel is waterlogged and rank. But the iron hoops are sound.
Packed to the lid with dark-binding crystal shards. Your hands go numb.

choices.label: Fish the floating crates instead

outcomes.text: Rope, sailcloth, a tin of flint. Honest salvage, no questions.
The crates split and empty. You burn an hour for one length of good line.
One crate is lashed to a corpse. You cut it loose and take the boots.

choices.label: Leave it. Escort sails

outcomes.text: You lie low. By dusk a grey topsail crosses the horizon and does not turn.
You watch the barrels drift onto the reef and break apart. A waste of good salt.
A UTC launch sweeps the flotsam and picks up your paddle trail.

history_note: Ships sighted Pedro Serrano's smoke for years but stayed clear of the shoals around his cay.

title: The Fin That Keeps Station
intro_lines: A triangular fin holds twenty yards off your quarter.
It has been there since noon.
It is not leaving.

choices.label: Bleed a fish and draw it away.

outcomes.text: You slit the fish and cast it wide. The fin turns aside, and the sea takes it.
The water boils where the fish lands. Two more fins come in from the west.
It takes the fish, then the line, then the knife out of your hand.

choices.label: Strike the water and shout at it.

outcomes.text: The fin sheers off. Bullies rarely want a fight they have to work for.
It circles closer, unhurried, and you run out of shouting.
It hits the raft from below. You cling to the lashings and count the seconds.

choices.label: Sit still. Keep your hands out

outcomes.text: By dusk the fin is gone. You sleep in shifts with the knife on your chest.
The waiting eats at you. Tide-Puck whines at the dark until dawn.
You doze. Something nudges the raft and you come up swinging at nothing.

history_note: Reef sharks are drawn by blood and thrashing in the shallows and tiger sharks work the dusk — a fin that keeps station is waiting for you to make one mistake.

title: Course by Cold Stars
intro_lines: No land, no light, no wind but the high cold air.
The stars come out hard and unfamiliar.
Tide-Puck faces north and will not turn.

choices.label: Steer by the stars Tide-Puck faces.

outcomes.text: You hold the line till grey light. At dawn, birds go low and landward.
You drift off the line in the dark and lose the whole night's work.
Cloud closes in. You have been steering at a lie for four hours.

choices.label: Heave to and wait for daylight.

outcomes.text: You sleep in turns and wake to a clean horizon. Nothing gained, nothing lost.
The current carries you somewhere in the dark. You do not like where.
A squall hits at three bells. You lose the mast step and a night's sleep.

choices.label: Light a lamp and watch for a sail.

outcomes.text: A far light answers yours, then winks out. A ship, or a trick of the swell.
You burn good tar for nothing. The dark stays exactly as dark.
A sail crosses your light and does not slow. False hope is its own wound.

history_note: The group who left Tromelin on a raft under a sail of woven feathers was never seen again — a course set without a landfall in mind is a course to nowhere.

title: Kraits in the Lashings
intro_lines: Something coils in the raft's lashings.
Two somethings.
Banded, pale-bellied, thick as your wrist.

choices.label: Cut them loose into the sea.

outcomes.text: The blade parts the lashing. Both snakes spill into the dark water.
One strikes your forearm as it falls. The bite burns, then goes numb.
You cut too deep and the raft's frame slackens. A bad trade for a worse night.

choices.label: Wait for them to leave on their own.

outcomes.text: By grey light they are gone, hunting the shallows. You slept not at all.
One slides across your leg in the dark. You do not move. It moves on.
One settles against your hip for warmth and stays until dawn.

choices.label: Ease them into a canvas sack, gently.

outcomes.text: You bag both and set them adrift. Careful work, and no bites taken.
One slips the sack and vanishes under the raft. The other you land.
A fang catches your knuckle through the cloth. Your hand swells by dawn.

history_note: Sea kraits are venomous but placid and come in at night — the bite almost always comes from a hand that grabs first and looks afterwards.

title: The Wake That Glows
intro_lines: Your paddle trail lights up blue, then fades.
Every ripple burns cold fire.
The sea is full of eyes.

choices.label: Paddle hard for the hum.

outcomes.text: The great light turns. In its wake, wreck-timber and a carved arch-stone drift free.
The hum passes a mile off. The swell lifts you and sets you down, gentle.
The wake hits like a wall. You lose the outrigger and a night's nerve.

choices.label: Keep still. Do not draw its eye.

outcomes.text: You sit in the dark while the hill of light crosses the horizon and is gone.
The hum circles twice, then dives. The sea goes black and utterly quiet.
It comes close enough to show the scars on its hide. You forget to breathe.

choices.label: Slap the water. Light the whole sea.

outcomes.text: The sea blooms white. You count three sharks and one very large shadow leaving.
The light brings a bull shark in fast. You beat it off with the paddle shaft.
The flare is so bright the dark ahead looks like a hole. You see nothing else.

history_note: Disturbed water glows with living light, and every predator in the reef reads disturbance as a dinner bell — sharks hunt by blood, thrashing and the smell of fear.

title: The Stranger's Tow
intro_lines: The stranger's boat returns with a line and a spare oar.
"You shared your water," he says.
"I pay what I owe." He ties on and starts to pull.

choices.label: Let him tow you to his camp.

outcomes.text: His camp is a careened sloop and four men. They feed you, then talk terms.
Three miles, then he casts off at the reef line. "That's as far as the water goes."
The tow-rope snaps in the swell and he is gone again, oars biting.

choices.label: Take the line, knife where he can see

outcomes.text: He laughs at the knife and tows you anyway. Trust, of a sort.
He tows you to a gutted hulk and asks payment in sailcloth.
He sees the knife and cuts the line himself. Fair enough, you suppose.

choices.label: Refuse the tow. Ask only for a heading.

outcomes.text: He gives you a bearing, a handful of dried fish, and goes.
He spits, gives you a heading, and you learn later it was a lie.
He gives you nothing but a long look and the stroke of his oar.

history_note: Serrano and his second castaway quarrelled bitterly before they made peace — the man you fed today may be the one who pulls you off the reef tomorrow.

title: The Knife in the Dark
intro_lines: He waited for dark, and for your eyes to get heavy.
The jug was a kindness.
The knife is not. Tide-Puck wakes you with a growl.

choices.label: Fight him. He is tired and you are

outcomes.text: You break his wrist against the mast step. He goes over the side.
He is faster than he looks. You take the cut and he takes your water.
You grapple, both go into the sea, and only one of you climbs back.

choices.label: Give him the water and let him go.

outcomes.text: He takes the jug, ashamed, and rows off. Word of it gets around.
He takes it, and then the oar as well. You watch him go.
He refuses, sets the jug down, and leaves you the fish he caught.

choices.label: Put Tide-Puck on him.

outcomes.text: Tide-Puck is on his arm before he can swing. He goes into the water screaming.
The little thing hesitates. He kicks it aside and is gone with your knife.
Tide-Puck holds him at the rail till dawn, then lets him take the dinghy.

history_note: Bartholomew Roberts' articles put a thief between mates ashore with his ears and nose slit — the sea's law assumes the man beside you may rob you.

title: The Wreck on the Reef
intro_lines: A three-master stands up on the reef, masts gone.
Her name-board reads MERIDIAN.
UTC charter.

choices.label: Board her from the lee side.

outcomes.text: Her forward hold is dry: powder, sailcloth, a chart case still latched.
The deck shifts under you. You take one crate and leave the rest.
A bulkhead gives. You come up under a fallen spar and lose skin getting out.

choices.label: Take the smoke for survivors. Shout.

outcomes.text: Two sailors in the chains, half-drowned. They weep when you cut them down.
No one answers. The smoke is a burning coal bunker and the heat drives you back.
A UTC officer, armed, does not want rescuing. He wants your raft.

choices.label: Strip the copper and leave her.

outcomes.text: Two sheets of copper and a keg of tallow, before the surf turns against you.
The reef takes your footing and opens your shin. You keep the copper.
A UTC patrol ketch rounds the headland with her colours up and her guns run out.

history_note: At Île Sainte-Marie ships were deliberately sunk as a harbour barrier and Condent burned the Fiery Dragon rather than see her sail — a wreck on a reef is salvage, trap and tomb at once.
